why: Senj baptisms, page 122, entry 96 gives the birth as 9 October and the baptism as 17 October. The tree's 19 is a transcription slip against the register it cites.

The 1920 marriage register, written in his lifetime from his baptismal certificate, gives 1892 1/III. The stone was cut after 1966 from memory. The archive follows the register and records the stone as wrong.

tree: Wife of Michael Žubrinić; mother of Nicolaus (b. 24 January 1834)
record: Born 8 September 1835 — twenty months after her supposed son
why: Her baptismal entry is real and hers: Otočac 1835, entry 41, daughter of Marcus Orešković adoptatus Sekula and Lucia née Sekula of Dubrava 29. The transcription is right and the attachment is wrong. Nicolaus's own 1834 entry names his mother as an Orešković, but an earlier one, still unidentified. Six further ancestors hang below this join.

tree: Asserted, with no document — this archive called it Disputed
record: Documented: Senj marriages, 8 December 1920, page 366 entry 41
why: The marriage entry names the groom's parents as Juraj Blažević and Tereza r. Žubrinić, and annotates them mrt. — deceased — which puts Juraj's death before December 1920. He remains undated and unplaced, and nothing yet links him to Toma above.

The Vrbnik baptisms for 1806, house 244, read: Die 14. Martii Ao 1806 baptizavi ego Michaël Kombol C.L. infantem lege natum patre Joanne, Matre Marthæ Antich Papa, nomine Josephum. The tree's date is exact. The entry also names his father Joannes (ahnentafel 48) and his mother Martha, and gives the godparents as the village judge Mathias Jellichich and his wife Margarita.

record: Josephus — and the priest wrote the accusative himself
why: The register reads nomine Josephum. That is the priest's own Latin, not a modern transcriber's slip: Michaël Kombol writes nomine followed by the accusative in every entry on the page — Mariam, Joannem, Matthæam, Magdalenam, Nicolaum. The tree copied the register faithfully and inherited its grammar.

The Karlobag register for August 1789 reads Mariam natam pridie ex Michaele et Lucia Gergacs. The register's spelling is Gergacs; Gerkacs is the secondary form and the tree carries it first. The entry also gives her mother as Lucia — written over a struck-out name — and her father as Michael.

record: August 1789, born the day before baptism — consistent
why: The entry says natam pridie, born the previous day, and sits in the August 1789 sequence after the entry of 9 August. That is consistent with 11 August but the scan does not itself carry a day number; the exact day comes from the index, not the page.

record: April 1777, Karlobag, born the day before — consistent
why: The Karlobag register reads: baptizavi Infantem heri natum ex Georgio et Maria Uroda Conjugibus hujus Loci, cui impositum est Nomen Joannis Georgij. It confirms the year, the place and both parents, and shows he was born the day before the baptism — but the page carries no day number, so 22 April comes from the index rather than the register. The godparents are Pro-Colonel Joannes Hallinich de Zirfeld and the wife of Captain Daniel de Hofenegg: Military Frontier officers standing for a Karlobag child.

what: She is not this child's mother
tree: Mother of Nicolaus Žubrinić, b. 24 January 1834
record: Born 8 September 1835 — nineteen months after him
why: The Otočac register of 24 January 1834 enters Nicolaus as the legitimate son of Michaël Xubrinich and Maria uxor ejus nata Oreskovich — a married woman bearing a legitimate child, nineteen months before Maria Catharina was born. Her own 1835 baptism names the same parents the tree gives her and places her at Dubrava N° 29, so she is a real person married here to the wrong man. The join is kept and marked rather than severed, because a wrong join is itself a finding and the only pointer to where the right Maria Orešković should be looked for.

Confiniarius, ex Pago Shumechicza N. 24 — a Military Frontier household at Šumećica house 24. Father Michaël Xubrinich; mother Maria, née Orešković. Godparents Petrus, son of Franciscus Xubrinich, retired Vigiliarum Magister, and Maria, wife of Joannes Xubrinich, Sylvarum Custos at Šumećica.

record: 1834: Maria nata Oreskovich · 1845: Maria nata Marković
why: The Otočac baptism of his son Josephus, 16 March 1845, gives the mother as Maria Žubrinić nata Marković; the 1834 baptism of Nicolaus gives Maria nata Orešković. Either the first wife died and he remarried a second Maria, or there are two men of this name — there are 68 Žubrinić records at Otočac. Nothing read so far chooses between them.
